summary:
An actual bounded read-only audit reconstructed verified context bundles for 13 of 16 fixed historical cases selected outside known development parent components and UTC week blocks. Two lacked a qualifying strictly earlier merge witness and one used an unsupported link/tree mode; every original outcome was retained without replacement or retry. This is limited feasibility evidence, not population coverage, a hardness predictor or cross-profile invariance.

Reconstruction uses exact creation requirements, strictly earlier server merge witnesses and local commit/tree/blob hashes. Git author dates do not prove visibility. Lazy promisor fetching must remain disabled; equal timestamp buckets cannot prove prior ordering. Later-event diagnostics stay controller-only: identical permitted evidence must yield identical rater artifacts despite later history. Pre-cutoff checkpoints may lag the actual branch state; creation may follow research or partial implementation, so remaining-work and total-demand targets differ. Private creator context, dependencies/runtime and actual work intervals remain incomplete.

Artifact separation is not qualified filesystem/network isolation; no rating or implementation trial was launched and no routing policy activated. Source/report publication and Root accepted reconstruction have distinct scopes. Raw cases/runtime evidence remain private with Programme/Root. The broader #5276/#5248 validity acceptance remains open.
title: Historical code context is reconstructible within explicit visibility and blinding limits
